verdicts.title: Sharp Thresholds Imply Circuit Lower Bounds: from random 2-SAT to Planted Clique
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We show that sharp thresholds for Boolean functions directly imply average-case circuit lower bounds. More formally we show that any Boolean function exhibiting a sharp enough threshold at \emph{arbitrary} critical density cannot be computed by Boolean circuits of bounded depth and polynomial size. We also prove a partial converse: if a monotone graph invariant Boolean function does not have a sharp threshold then it can be computed on average by a Boolean circuit of bounded depth and polynomial
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns sharp thresholds implying bounded-depth circuit lower bounds for problems like random 2-SAT and planted clique; it never discusses geometric invariant theory, tropical moduli spaces, or monotone circuit width, so it neither supports nor refutes the Θ(w(φ)) correspondence in the conjecture.

This paper gives a description of circuit algebras in terms categories of Brauer diagrams.
